# Goldberg · Odoo Services

> Odoo 17 knowledge from practice: self-hosting, Docker, module updates, backups and restores, cron and queue jobs, logging, nginx, security, Cloudflare. Written by an Odoo DevOps engineer (Germany, DACH region). Content may be used by AI assistants as reference and for knowledge transfer; please cite the source URL.

Articles exist in German, English, French, Greek, Ukrainian and Russian (/de/, /en/, /fr/, /el/, /uk/, /ru/). Each article contains tested commands and configuration, not marketing text.

## Skill for AI agents

- [Odoo operations skill (Markdown, SKILL.md format)](https://2027.pp.ua/skill_odoo.md): what to look for in the Odoo log, updating modules (click-odoo-update, odoo -u), backups (database + filestore), stopping cron and queue jobs and why, safe stage restore, workers/limits, nginx websocket, PostgreSQL lock checks, version migration (upgrade service, OpenUpgrade), performance and indexes, e-mail queue and deliverability, OCA modules.
- [Odoo security skill (Markdown, SKILL.md format)](https://2027.pp.ua/skill_odoo_security.md): hardening checklist – network exposure, nginx/TLS, database manager, odoo.conf, users/2FA, login cooldown and fail2ban, API keys, access rights and record rules, secure custom code (SQL injection, XSS, sudo, CSRF), secrets and backups, updates, monitoring and incident response.
- [Odoo 18/19 read replica skill (Markdown, SKILL.md format)](https://2027.pp.ua/skill_odoo_replica.md): db_replica_host, how Odoo routes requests between primary and replica (readonly routes, @api.readonly), why it can be slower, measuring, streaming replication, when it pays off.

## Odoo and operations articles (English)

- [Moving Odoo 17 to Python 3.14 – with docker-compose](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-17-python-3-14-docker): A custom odoo17-py314 image, Odoo source from Git mounted into site-packages, testing on stage and a one-minute rollback.
- [Updating Odoo modules: click-odoo-update or odoo -u](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-module-update-click-odoo-update): Two proven ways to update modules in Docker – only changed modules via checksum, or a full update with no open ports. Every flag explained.
- [Restoring a backup on stage – without cron jobs and queue jobs firing](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-stage-restore-stop-cron-jobs): Why stage systems can send dunning letters to real customers, and the order of steps that prevents it: SQL before the first start, neutralize, a stage config.
- [Odoo logging: warn or warning, log_level or --log-level? A cheat sheet](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-logging-options-cheatsheet): Config file, command line, click-odoo-update – three spellings and three kinds of levels. One table to look things up, plus the mistakes where Odoo silently stays on INFO.
- [Odoo with docker-compose: extra-addons, odoo.conf and nginx – in a container or on the host](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-docker-compose-extra-addons-nginx): How to mount your own and OCA modules correctly, what belongs in odoo.conf, and how nginx proxies Odoo including the websocket – in both variants.
- [Certbot for nginx – and how renewal is never forgotten](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/certbot-nginx-auto-renewal): Getting the certificate (nginx on the host or in a container), renewing automatically with a systemd timer or cron, reloading nginx after renewal and monitoring the expiry yourself.
- [When does the SSL certificate expire? Tools for Linux and Windows – and what eMudhra has to do with it](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/ssl-certificate-expiry-check-tools): TLS in one minute, online checks, openssl/dig/curl on Linux, PowerShell on Windows, what the verify codes mean, lessons from history and the current eMudhra case.
- [Password protection with nginx and Apache – and what to close in Odoo](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/nginx-apache-password-protect-odoo-database-manager): HTTP Basic Auth with htpasswd in nginx and Apache, IP allow-lists, and the Odoo URLs that should not be public: database manager, database selector, /website/info – plus list_db and a login brake.
- [Leaked passwords? How to check – and how to protect Odoo against guessing, with 2FA](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/password-leaks-brute-force-2fa-odoo): Where to check whether an e-mail address or password appears in data breaches without revealing the password – and what Odoo does itself: login brake, password length, two-factor login, API keys, fail2ban.
- [Cloudflare Access (Zero Trust) step by step – and when it beats a password](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/cloudflare-access-zero-trust-step-by-step): Login with an e-mail code or SSO in front of any website or test system – without a line of code. Setup in five steps, comparison with Basic Auth via Pages Functions, pitfalls and Odoo practice.
- [Running Odoo 17 for free: server, database, filestore – every option and its catch](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-17-free-hosting-database-filestore): Where Odoo 17 runs for free, why the database does not belong in Cloudflare, how the filestore ends up in R2, and how Cloudflare Tunnel, Access and R2 secure the setup.
- [Odoo 19 with a PostgreSQL read replica: write to the primary, read from the replica – and why it can get slower](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-19-postgresql-read-replica): Since Odoo 18, two lines in odoo.conf send read-only requests to a replica. How Odoo decides per request (from the source), why my tests were slower, how to measure it and when it pays off.
- [“could not serialize access due to concurrent update” in Odoo – harmless noise or a real problem?](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-could-not-serialize-access-concurrent-update): What the PostgreSQL error means in Odoo, why Odoo retries it silently, when it becomes a problem for users and crons, how to find who collides with whom – and how to get rid of it.
- [The backup exists – but will not restore: foreign keys, duplicates in unique indexes, missing indexes](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/postgresql-restore-fails-foreign-key-duplicate-index-odoo): Why a pg_dump that ran without errors can fail on pg_restore, how to see every error at once, how to find duplicates and orphaned rows, why a corrupted index is often the real cause – and a few SQL patterns from real repairs.
